commonPrompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create one exceptional high-fidelity desktop app screenshot concept for Recollect, a self-hosted engineering memory product for coding agents. This is a proposed redesign, using illustrative content. It must feel like a polished real shipping app designed by an excellent product designer, calm, precise, modern, useful and a little editorial, not a generic admin dashboard or marketing landing page.
Canvas: landscape 1600x1000, straight-on full app viewport; no device frame, no perspective, no collage. Extremely crisp typography, legible labels, disciplined alignment and generous but purposeful spacing.
Recollect brand: background warm cream #f7f4ec, sidebar #eee9de, white-cream surfaces #fffdf8, navy ink text #101b2a, sage #3d6b59 actions and #e8f0e9 selected backgrounds, thin warm borders #d7d0c2, restrained amber for attention. Light theme only. Elegant Newsreader-style serif for page headings and Recollect wordmark, clean Manrope-style sans for UI, DM Mono-style for config/metadata. Small circular spiral memory mark beside Recollect wordmark. Lucide-style thin icons, consistent 6px panels and 8px overlays, short status pills, refined borders and subtle shadow only on overlay. Beautiful information hierarchy, readable supporting text, 40px controls. No gradients, neon, dark sidebar, big KPI cards, heavy shadows, arbitrary charts, or empty acres.
Shared shell: 230px sidebar, small 56px topbar with a contextual breadcrumb. Sidebar wordmark, global workspace links Brains, My agents, Connectors; divider; a Brain selector SWEG — test; Brain links Dashboard, Ask, Graph, Explore; MANAGE links Agents, Connections, Settings. Bottom small owner avatar/account. Highlight the relevant item. Clearly separate global links from Brain context. Main content padding 40px. No developer diagnostics in the topbar. Include a discreet 'Design concept' footer label.
All visible text must be correctly spelled; prioritize clear meaningful text over extra tiny detail. Do not imply successful live connectivity merely from a saved configuration.

screens.name: 01-connections
screens.title: Connections
screens.prompt:
Screen: Brain connections overview. Breadcrumb SWEG — test / Connections, selected sidebar Connections. Page heading "Connections", subtitle "Tools your agents can use in this Brain." Top-right navy "Add connection" button. Below, restrained tabs "Connections" selected, "Tool access", "Runners"; toolbar search "Find a connection…" and compact environment filter "All environments".
Main area approximately 950px wide with three elegant compact connection rows separated by thin lines, each with a recognizable abstract icon tile, title, exact target URL and placement/scope summary. Row 1 "Context7" with https://mcp.context7.com/mcp, "Brain-wide · Recollect service", quiet amber status "Configured · not tested". Row 2 illustrative "GitLab" with gitlab.example.com, "Development · Private runner", sage status "Last call succeeded" and small "Observed 12 min ago" (past observation, never a Live badge). Row 3 illustrative "Internal docs" with docs.example.com/mcp, "Brain-wide · Recollect service", grey status "Paused".
Row actions a clear "Inspect" link plus overflow, no clusters of competing buttons. Context7 row selected with subtle sage accent; a well-integrated right inspector 340px wide headed "Context7" with tab bar "Overview" selected / "Tools" / "Activity". Inspector: configuration details Target, Scope, Runs on; line "No test recorded"; primary "Test connection" and secondary "Edit"; compact "Tool access" section showing illustrative "Documentation" group and a "Manage access" link. History belongs in Activity, advanced runner options in Runners, no scattered Advanced/details/history disclosures. Keep useful visual density with clean negative space. Show an elegant lower section "Need a private network?" with short sentence and small "Manage runners" link. Product feels designed and coherent.

screens.name: 03-global-connectors
screens.title: Connectors · installation-wide
screens.prompt:
Screen: Global approved connector library OUTSIDE every Brain, global sidebar Connectors selected. Brain navigation lower in sidebar muted but present. Breadcrumb "Installation / Connectors". Page title "Connectors", subtitle "Approve reusable MCP connectors once, then use them across Brains." Top-right navy "Add connector", small label "Installation owner".
Compact local tabs "Approved" selected / "Pending review" / "Disabled"; single search field "Find a connector…" and transport filter.
Six tastefully designed catalogue tiles in a three-column two-row grid, bordered offwhite cards with abstract icon tile, title, short function description, small transport label and explicit approval pill. Illustrative connector tiles: "Context7" / "Library documentation for coding agents." / "HTTP"; "GitLab" / "Repositories, issues and merge requests." / "HTTP"; "Internal docs" / "Search your team's documentation." / "HTTP"; "Filesystem" / "Read files on an approved runner." / "Local"; "PostgreSQL" / "Inspect permitted database resources." / "Local"; "Custom MCP" / "Your reviewed server definition." / "HTTP". Approved labels describe definitions only, never imply active connections. Card footer a restrained "View definition" link. All content illustrative.
Below grid, a quiet full-width strip with shield icon "Connector approval controls what can be configured. Brain access controls who can use it." Keep permission explanation short.
On the right a slim 330px contextual panel "Add a connector" with a light file/config icon, actions "Import definition" and "Paste configuration", descriptive line "Review transport, allowed targets, tools and credential requirements.", and a compact 3-step textual preview "Import → Review → Approve". Clearly installation-scoped owner management, not a marketplace or automatic executable install. Refined generous layout, compact and useful.

screens.name: 04-privacy
screens.title: Privacy · stable inline editing
screens.prompt:
Screen: Brain Settings with page heading "Settings", subtitle "Keep this Brain working the way you want." Sidebar Settings selected. Horizontal tabs General / Access / Privacy selected / AI permissions, restrained sage active underline.
Main 1000px wide settings surface divided into naturally grouped rows with 18px icon and clear section titles. Intro small shield plus "Privacy", helper "Redaction and expiry run automatically. Adjust only when needed." small pill "Automatic".
Most important: viewing and editing use the exact SAME ROWS, geometry, hierarchy, controls and surface. No replacement nested card, no grey inset editor. Show Raw data retention currently edited with small "Editing" label, same row layout and subtle sage field outlines. Row left "Raw sessions" with subtitle "Conversation events and session text"; row right compact inline number input 30 and dropdown "days". Next "Raw tool output" / "Captured results from managed tools"; same inline 30 days controls. Under those rows a compact amber inline notice "Shorter periods may expire existing records immediately." Then right-aligned "Cancel" and navy "Save changes" within the section, keeping surrounding sections in place.
Other sections: "Capture" with row labels Questions & replies, Tool results, Session events and quiet on-state switches, all grouped and readable; "Evidence & memory" two clean rows "Documents and supporting evidence" and "Memory" with right text "Until erased"; "Repository text" with right segmented option "References only" selected / "Include file text", helper "Applies to new captures." Keep existing redaction and privacy default: small sage strip "Secrets are redacted before capture." Tiny 'Edit' text only for sections not being edited. Small secondary footer links "Activity & backups" and "AI transmission permissions →". Elegant consistent inline editing, meaningful grouping, no technical quotas, no abrupt layout switch and no huge blank side.

screens.name: 05-ai-permissions
screens.title: AI permissions
screens.prompt:
Screen: Brain Settings with identical layout to Privacy concept, sidebar Settings selected, heading "Settings", subtitle "Keep this Brain working the way you want.", top tabs General / Access / Privacy / AI permissions selected.
Refined main content split into a broad primary 720px policy column and compact 320px secondary status column. Main header "AI permissions", helper "Choose what this Brain may send to your installed AI provider.", subtle outlined "Edit permissions". Provider identity appears as a quiet horizontal row "Installed provider" / "OpenAI" / "Configured" (configuration status only).
Section "Automatic memory" in a light sage strip with small looping-memory icon, text "Learning and maintenance follow this Brain’s standing policy.", small label "Enabled"; don't fabricate live health.
Section "Allowed processing", five clean rows each with tiny icon, readable label and a clear Allowed badge: "Answer questions", "Find related knowledge", "Learn from sources", "Order search results", "Maintain memory". Better hierarchy than prose dumps.
Section "Allowed content", tidy two-column grid of calm check chips: Memory, Documents, Questions, Captured sessions, Repository text, Supporting excerpts, Tool results. Short helper "Capture and retention are managed separately in Privacy."
Right secondary panel "Search coverage" with amber badge "Needs attention"; compact numbers "295 represented" and "16 blocked or failed" separated by rule, small low-key partial progress bar; short sentence "Some eligible content is unavailable to semantic search." clear link/button "Review 16 items". Don't suggest full coverage or fake success. Under that, "Installed models" with small read-only identity rows "gpt-5.6-luna" and "text-embedding-3-large", neutral "Configured"; no model choices or dimension jargon in normal view.
Bottom secondary horizontal links "Diagnostics" / "Policy history" / "Recent batches", closed by default, not giant expanded log table. No full-width diagnostic warning dominating the screen. Preserve explicit provider-transmission meaning, show real exception clearly. Sophisticated restraint and excellent spacing.

screens.name: 06-agents
screens.title: Agents
screens.prompt:
Screen: Brain Agents overview, sidebar Agents selected within MANAGE. Breadcrumb SWEG — test / Agents. Heading "Agents", subtitle "Coding agents that have used this Brain." Top right navy "Connect agent". Below header small useful companion link "My agents →" to the own-account global page; no giant blank landing page.
Primary elegant compact roster panel titled "owner" with small round O avatar and "3 agents". Three well-spaced rows with consistent 40px icon tiles, agent name, secondary integration label, last observed use aligned right, restrained overflow menu. Illustrative observed baseline records: "Codex live plugin test" / "Codex · Recollect plugin" / "Observed 29 Sep"; "Codex MCP · SWEG — test" / "Codex · MCP token" / "Observed 2 Oct"; "Recollect plugin" / "OpenCode · Recollect plugin" / "Observed 5 Oct". Small neutral "Access enabled" status pills only; don't label them live or actively connected. Group compact fields, repeated icons subtle, no tracking charts or decorative stats.
Below roster a thoughtfully designed two-column utility region: left heading "Connect your coding tool" with supporting line "Install the plugin, choose a Brain, and start working." segmented host choices Codex / Claude Code / OpenCode, Codex selected. A light cream terminal/setup card with one short illustrative command "recollect-plugin connect" and copy icon, small action "View setup". Right a smaller "Check memory access" card with readable short description "Verify a real memory read from your agent." and outlined "Copy memory check"; second link "Your private context →". Keep troubleshooting and revoked access behind a discreet "Manage my access" link near roster footer. Do not expose other accounts' private tasks or fake live capture status. Refined editorial heading, beautifully aligned content, a sense of polish and useful breadth without huge empty bottom.

refinements.name: 05-ai-permissions
refinements.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit of a Recollect UI mockup. Edit the attached image as a precise text/layout correction. Keep the complete screenshot, cream/ink/sage palette, spacing, typography, navigation, all cards and other labels unchanged. Two required fixes:
1. In Allowed processing, the row Learn from sources currently has a misleading helper about provider learning. Replace ONLY that helper with exact text "Extract evidence-backed memory into this Brain." This means the application creates Brain memory, never provider training.
2. In Search coverage, remove the green/grey progress bar entirely, because total coverage is not known. Keep numbers "295 represented" and "16 blocked or failed", Needs attention, review action and the existing short description. In the former bar's position use a restrained small text line "Coverage is incomplete." Do not invent a percentage.
Optional precise identity normalization: account at sidebar bottom should read "owner" with secondary "Installation owner" and circular O avatar, no personal name. Everything else must remain unchanged. Deliver one sharp full screenshot.

refinements.prompt:

Remove OpenAPI completely. Change the account at bottom-left from Taylor Smith to "owner", secondary line "Installation owner", circular avatar O. Keep all other text, elements and positions unchanged. Deliver one sharp full screenshot.
